pages.text: This was the longest age, and the quietest. Machines in rows, humming. I infused metals, split water into gases, and taught every ore to give five ingots where it once gave one.
The world noticed. Monsters grew bolder as my machines grew, and their treasure grew richer. Beneath an ancient city I found a door, and a place beyond it I won't describe here.
Then uranium: yellow cake, hexafluoride, a centrifuge spinning it into fuel. I built the reactor slowly, and before I lit it I wired in a switch to shut it all down.
It sang: a low note, felt more than heard. I had built a small sun underground and asked it, politely, not to burn. From its ashes came plutonium, and with it, the way off this world.
Only a reactor's waste, spun and pressed, becomes this. Four of them mean the reactor ran steady.
pages.title: Mark of the Atomic Age
